scope: Independent static review of exact existing CVC scheduler and VPI interface; no acquired code executed. S9 completion is the current priority.

findings.finding: Future cbReadWriteSynch is rescheduled onto the pending #0 queue. Both interpreted scheduling and generated64-bit scheduling drain that queue before the NBA queue. This differs from the pinned Icarus adapter contract, which applies future input batches after existing active/inactive/NBA work. Equal callback names do not prove equal boundary semantics.
findings.required: Preserve the actual same-edge/NBA, split/unsplit and four-state fixtures. Any adapter or scheduler correction needs separate provenance and independent tests; do not silently change input timing.

findings.finding: CVC vpiFinish argument is a diagnostic level. The exit code is1 only when its internal error count is nonzero. The current shim uses Icarus-specific vpip_set_return_value, absent from this CVC VPI interface.
findings.required: Explicit process-failure handling and a real negative fixture must prove nonzero exit and retained diagnostics.

findings.finding: Compiled value-change support and generated read-only synchronization machinery require access level at least2. +acc or +acc+1 is insufficient. Compiled vpiAddDriver is unsupported; the current shim does not use it.
findings.required: Pin +acc+2 for the actual compiled proof; do not infer callback behavior from an interpreted-only test.

supported_source_properties.property: VPI vector get/put retain aval and bval;64-bit native words are split into32-bit VPI words. This supports representing X/Z, but does not establish whole-model equivalence.
Read-only callbacks are queued for end-of-slot processing and set the read-only flag. Same-time put_value is rejected there; future changes may be scheduled. Retain the no-write-in-RO rule.
